attributes.title: tag_rename
attributes.description: Rename a Tag or Folder inside its own parent via system.tag.rename with the handler-fixed Abort collision policy, with the D30 2 Tag config fingerprint as the per-target Precondition token. Each item carries the target path, the new name and the tcf1 fingerprint of that target's own tag_get_config read. The new name is one path segment: a rename never changes the parent, so the new path is the old parent plus the new name, and that is what D30 6 measures against the tag_rename Target allowlist (a UDT definition only under an explicit _types_ entry). Reads the Runtime Target Policy first and fails closed with operation_disabled when it is missing or unusable. Owner ruling 1 still covers both ends: either the target or the new path inside the reserved IgnitionMCPPolicy provider is refused with permission_denied whatever the allowlist says, including an explicit *, before the allowlist is consulted. Preflight validates every item's input, the new path's Target, the target's existence and fingerprint, and the new path's absence before any item executes: a stale fingerprint is conflict, a target that is not there is not_found, and an occupied new path is conflict, so nothing is ever overwritten. After Preflight the items execute one at a time with no rollback and the Native QualityCode of each system.tag.rename call is that item's outcome; a new path that appears between the fingerprints and the dispatch aborts that item - conflict, never a success. Observed state is the new path present and the old path absent. Runtime audit follows the policy's auditMode; a failed post-Mutation audit write gives auditRecorded=false, never a failure. Every request is bounded (D10): 20 targets by default up to the 100-target hard maximum, and the deployment may raise the default through tagRenameMaxItems in the Runtime Target Policy; both the target path and the new path have finite ceilings, an over-budget request is a limit_exceeded refusal before any native call, and a caller that wants to change a parent uses tag_move. A refused Target or Precondition writes one Runtime audit decision row (none in off mode, fail-closed in required mode).

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: 1..100 rename items: {"path": provider-qualified Tag or Folder path to rename, "newName": the new name, one path segment with no / and no wildcard, "expectedFingerprint": the tcf1 fingerprint from tag_get_config for that exact path}. The target must exist with that fingerprint and the new path must not exist, or the whole batch is refused before anything is renamed. Default 20 (D10), hard maximum 100.
